provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Athletics: baton relay
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the rules of baton relay.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper baton passing.
Introduction:
We have learned about running in our previous classes. Today we will learn how to pass a baton in a relay race.
Content:
Baton relay is a team race where runners pass a short stick called a baton. The runner must hold the baton in their right hand and pass it to the next runner's left hand. If you drop the baton, your team can pick it up but you lose time. Like passing a yam in the market, you must be careful not to drop it.
Class activity:
Divide the class into four teams. Set up a relay course in the school field. Let each team practice passing the baton without dropping it.
Evaluation questions:
What is a baton?
How many hands should you use to hold the baton?
What happens if you drop the baton?
Summary:
Baton relay teaches teamwork and careful passing of the baton between runners.

topics.title: Ball games: football
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate dribbling a football.
The pupils should be able to explain the rules of a mini match.
Introduction:
We have played with balls before. Today we will learn how to dribble and pass a football like our favorite players.
Content:
Dribbling means kicking the ball while running. Use the inside of your foot to control the ball. Passing means kicking the ball to your teammate. In a mini match, we play on a small field with few rules. No pushing other players. Like playing in the compound, we must share the ball and play fair.
Class activity:
Set up a small football field. Let pupils practice dribbling around cones. Then divide into teams for a mini match.
Evaluation questions:
What is dribbling?
How do you pass a football?
What is one rule of the mini match?
Summary:
Football teaches us to control the ball and work together as a team.

topics.title: Gymnastics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform a forward roll.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate a balancing position.
Introduction:
We have learned about different body movements. Today we will learn rolling and balancing like gymnasts.
Content:
Rolling means to roll your body on the mat. For a forward roll, tuck your chin to your chest and push off with your legs. Balancing means to hold a position without falling. Try to balance on one foot like a flamingo. Always land with bent knees to protect your back. Like the harmattan season, we must be steady and not fall down.
Class activity:
Set up mats in the classroom. Let pupils practice forward rolls and balancing positions.
Evaluation questions:
How do you do a forward roll?
What part of your body should you bend when landing?
How long can you balance on one foot?
Summary:
Gymnastics helps us learn body control and safe movement.

topics.title: Posture and body care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper sitting posture.
The pupils should be able to explain why back care is important.
Introduction:
We sit and stand every day. Today we will learn how to sit, stand and walk properly to care for our backs.
Content:
Good posture means sitting with your back straight and shoulders back. When standing, keep your feet apart for balance. Walking well means swinging your arms and looking forward. Your back has many small bones that need care. Like carrying a bucket of water on your head, you must keep your back straight to avoid pain.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice sitting properly at their desks. Then walk around the classroom with good posture.
Evaluation questions:
What is good sitting posture?
Why is back care important?
How should you walk properly?
Summary:
Good posture helps us stay healthy and avoid back pain.

topics.title: Disease prevention
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list clean habits that prevent sickness.
The pupils should be able to explain how to prevent malaria.
Introduction:
We all want to stay healthy. Today we will learn how clean habits can stop us from getting sick.
Content:
Clean habits include washing hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet. Cover your mouth when coughing or sneezing. To prevent malaria, sleep under a treated net. Malaria comes from mosquitoes that bite at night. Like closing the windows during harmattan, we must protect ourselves from mosquitoes.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice proper handwashing technique. Then demonstrate how to hang a mosquito net properly.
Evaluation questions:
Name one clean habit that prevents sickness.
How do we prevent malaria?
What happens if we don't wash our hands?
Summary:
Clean habits and mosquito nets help us stay healthy and prevent diseases.

topics.title: Safety in school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list playground rules.
The pupils should be able to explain why no pushing at stairs is important.
Introduction:
School should be a safe place for everyone. Today we will learn rules that keep us safe at school.
Content:
Playground rules include taking turns on the slide and not pushing others. When using stairs, walk carefully and hold the rail. No running on wet floors. Like danfo drivers, we must follow traffic rules to avoid accidents. Pushing at stairs can cause serious falls and injuries.
Class activity:
Let pupils demonstrate safe behavior on stairs and on the playground equipment.
Evaluation questions:
What is one playground rule?
Why should we not push at stairs?
How should we walk on wet floors?
Summary:
Following safety rules helps prevent accidents and injuries at school.

topics.title: Swimming and water safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state pool rules.
The pupils should be able to explain why never swim alone is important.
Introduction:
Water can be fun but also dangerous. Today we will learn how to stay safe when swimming.
Content:
Pool rules include no running near the water and no pushing others in. Always swim with an adult watching. Never swim alone because you might get into trouble. Like crossing a busy road, you need help to stay safe. If you cramp, call for help immediately.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice calling for help in water. Then demonstrate safe entering and exiting of the pool.
Evaluation questions:
What is one pool rule?
Why should we never swim alone?
What should you do if you cramp in water?
Summary:
Water safety rules help prevent accidents and drowning in swimming pools.

topics.title: Traditional games
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two local children games.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to play one traditional game.
Introduction:
Our parents played games when they were young. Today we will learn and play some traditional Nigerian games.
Content:
Traditional games include Ayo (counting seeds) and Police and Thief. In Ayo, players move seeds around holes in a board. Police and Thief involves chasing and tagging. These games teach us about our culture and help us make friends. Like sharing kolanuts at ceremonies, these games bring us together.
Class activity:
Let pupils play Ayo and Police Thief in small groups. Rotate so everyone tries both games.
Evaluation questions:
Name one traditional game.
How do you play Ayo?
What skills do traditional games teach us?
Summary:
Traditional games connect us to our culture and teach important skills.

topics.title: First aid
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate simple bandaging.
The pupils should be able to identify items in a first aid box.
Introduction:
Sometimes we get small injuries. Today we will learn how to help ourselves and others with first aid.
Content:
First aid is help given when someone is hurt. For small cuts, clean the wound and cover with a bandage. A first aid box contains bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and scissors. Like fixing a broken pot with glue, we can fix small injuries with first aid. Always tell an adult about serious injuries.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice bandaging a doll's arm. Then identify items in a first aid box.
Evaluation questions:
What is first aid?
Name one item in a first aid box.
How do you treat a small cut?
Summary:
First aid helps us treat small injuries and know when to get adult help.

topics.title: Revision and sports day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to participate in class mini sports.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate one skill learned this term.
Introduction:
We have learned many skills this term. Today we will practice them and have a fun sports day.
Content:
Class mini sports include relay races, football matches and gymnastics displays. We will show what we learned about baton relay, football, rolling and balancing. Like celebrating the end of harvest, sports day is a time to celebrate our hard work. Everyone will get a certificate for participating.
Class activity:
Organize mini sports events where pupils can demonstrate skills learned during the term.
Evaluation questions:
What is your favorite sport from this term?
What skill have you improved most?
How do you feel about sports day?
Summary:
Sports day lets us show our skills and celebrate our learning this term.
